author: picklerickursion
text: Are you still paying $10 just to read the second half of a coding tutorial? 🧠 You are falling for a "client-side illusion." Rick shows Morty how to use the Developer Tools to disable JavaScript and remove the digital cardboard blocking the text that's already sitting in your RAM. Stop renting the internet and start owning it. (Plus, knowing simple tricks like this is exactly how you start building a massive faceless tech audience). 🚀 Deep Dive Description The Illusion: Many news sites and tutorial blogs use "Soft Paywalls." Instead of keeping the article on their secure server, they send the entire text to your browser, and then use a simple JavaScript code to trigger a popup overlay that hides it. The DevTools Hack:You don't need a credit card to bypass a client-side block; you just need to turn off the script doing the hiding. Press F12 to open Developer Tools. Press Ctrl + Shift + P to open the Command Menu. Type Disable JavaScript and hit Enter. Refresh the page. The popup will fail to load, leaving the raw text fully readable. The Catch: Modern web apps (like Twitter, YouTube, or Discord) rely entirely on JavaScript to function. If you leave it disabled, the modern internet will break and look like a blank page from 1995. You must repeat the steps and type Enable JavaScript when you are done reading. The Creator Pivot: You already know how to code, cook, or troubleshoot. If you screen-record simple solutions like this without ever showing your face, you can turn your basic competence into a highly monetized digital asset. Teach what you know. text: How I build with Astra 6 👇 Academy in bio 🔗 The architectural drawing look, works for any product or studio site: 1. Blueprint grid: repeating-linear-gradient in both directions, 1px lines at rgba(0,0,0,.06), 40px apart, on a fixed background layer 3. Corner crosshairs: a small + drawn with two 1px pseudo elements, absolutely placed at each corner of the frame. This one detail sells the whole thing 4. Hairlines only: 1px borders, never rounded, and ONE accent color used at 5% of the page 5. text: System design has many terms that sound similar… …but they solve very different problems. Here’s the simplest breakdown worth saving: LATENCY How long does one request take? THROUGHPUT How many requests can the system process over time? BANDWIDTH How much data can move through the network at once? — REPLICATION Copies the same data across multiple machines. SHARDING Splits different parts of the data across multiple machines. — POLLING Keeps asking: “Has anything changed?” WEBHOOK Automatically sends a notification when something happens. — PROCESS An independent program with its own memory. THREAD A smaller execution unit that shares memory within a process. — LOAD BALANCER Distributes traffic across multiple servers. API GATEWAY Controls how clients access APIs. — CONCURRENCY Handles multiple tasks during the same period. PARALLELISM Executes multiple tasks at exactly the same time. — MONOLITH Built and deployed as one complete application. MICROSERVICES Split into smaller services that can be developed and deployed independently. Small differences. Big impact when designing production systems. Save this for your system design and AI engineering interviews. . . . text: #мем #programming #it #programminghumor #истории  «Пэтриот» (англ. Patriot, с англ. — «патриот», войсковой индекс — MIM-104) — американский зенитный ракетный комплекс большого радиуса действия, состоящий на вооружении Армии США и армий ряда других стран. Производится группой американских компаний во главе с «Рэйтеон». Комплекс «Пэтриот» создавался для замены зенитно-ракетных комплексов «Найк Геркулес» и «Хок» в качестве универсального средства противовоздушной обороны позиционных районов войск на средних и больших высотах. Помимо этого, Patriot должен был обеспечивать противоракетную оборону (ПРО) на уровне армии США. В октябре 1980 года был подписан контракт на производство серийной партии комплексов и ракет, в декабре 1981 года начались поставки в войска. На вооружение принят в 1982 году. Официальное словесное название комплекса является бэкронимом от фразы англ. Phased Array Tracking Radar to Intercept On Target ([комплекс, сопряжённый с] РЛС сопровождения c фазированной антенной решёткой для перехвата цели по линии визирования). В войсках за характерный вид контейнерной пусковой установки комплекс неформально называют «мусоровоз с гидроприводом» (dumpster on hydraulics). В настоящий момент эксплуатируется и поставляется в другие страны усовершенствованная версия системы, «Patriot» PAC-3. Цена поставки 9 батарей (по 4 ПУ на батарею) систем «Пэтриот» может доходить до 9 млрд $ (включает в себя 36 ПУ ЗУР «Пэтриот» PAC-3 (9 батарей по 4 ПУ), 288 ЗУР «Пэтриот» PAC-3, 216 ЗУР с усовершенствованным наведением GEM-T, 10 комплектов РЛС с фазированной решёткой, 10 контрольных станций захвата цели). Стоимость пуска одной ракеты составляет от 3 до 8 млн долл. США в зависимости от типа ракеты.

author: rick.theengineer
text: Most teams don't break production because they're bad at code. They break it because a human had to remember every step. SSH into the server. Pull the latest code. Install. Build. Copy files. Restart. Hope nothing breaks. Forget one step, like the database migration, and the site goes down with a 502 error. That's the problem CI/CD solves. It has two halves: CI (Continuous Integration) answers one question: is this code safe to merge? Every push runs the same pipeline automatically. It installs dependencies, runs the linter, runs unit and integration tests, builds the app and scans for vulnerabilities. If one check fails, the pipeline turns red and that code can't be merged until it's fixed. CD answers a different question: can we safely release it? The tested code becomes a release artifact (often a Docker image). It goes to staging first, where more checks run, and then on to production. Here's the part most people mix up: → Continuous DELIVERY: a human still clicks "deploy" before production. → Continuous DEPLOYMENT: if every check passes, it ships automatically. No human needed. And when something still goes wrong, good pipelines don't just ask "did the server start?" They ask "are health checks passing?" They roll out to 5% of users first (a canary), then 25%, 50%, 100%, and they roll back the moment error rates spike. Everything in this video comes from a real run: real commits, real test results, a real failing test (expected $3.56, got $4), and a real GitHub Actions workflow file. The real point of CI/CD isn't speed. It's that every release follows the exact same steps, every single time. Watch it to the end: the bug that brings production down at the end is the step that got forgotten at the start 👀 Save this for your next system design interview, and send it to the friend who still deploys over SSH. Which side does your team run: delivery or deployment? 👇 #cicd #devops #githubactions #softwareengineering #coding

author: kodekloud
text: Why Git Wasn’t Enough for Anthropic!! Anthropic’s AI agents merge over 30,000 code updates every single day, triggering a staggering 25 million automated testing jobs. Under standard Git, every single test machine had to clone gigabytes of repository history just to verify a one-file bug fix, generating an unsustainable 600 petabytes of network traffic daily. Because Git was designed decades ago for offline human developers who download an entire codebase to their local laptops, it completely buckled under the rapid-fire demands of automated AI development. To eliminate this bottleneck, Anthropic built Scion, a custom version control system where full code history stays on central servers while test runners fetch only the exact folder they need. Using content-based file IDs paired with smart multi-tier caching, Scion answers over 99% of file requests instantly, slashing checkout times from minutes to seconds and saving 25% of testing CPU power. Incredibly, a tiny team of just seven engineers built the entire replacement system using Claude in only five months. #SystemDesign #Anthropic #DevOps #SoftwareEngineering #AIEngineering #TechNews

author: kodekloud
text: How DNS Works Step by Step Many people assume DNS is a single massive database containing every website's IP address, but it is actually a global distributed hierarchy. When you type google.com, your computer first checks your browser's cache and your operating system's shared cache. If neither knows the address, your computer asks a recursive resolver provided by your internet provider. To locate an unknown domain, this resolver queries the Root servers at the top of the internet, which point it to the servers running the .com registry, which then redirect the request directly to Google's authoritative name server. Google's authoritative server holds the official records and hands back the exact IP address, allowing your browser to finally start its connection. Although querying multiple servers for a single website sounds slow, aggressive caching at every single layer ensures your resolver rarely needs to start from the top, resolving most web lookups in just a few milliseconds. author: legitalgorithmswithpeter
text: 🤯 Your computer can’t calculate 0.1 + 0.2 correctly. And a similar rounding error once contributed to the deaths of 28 soldiers. Here’s why. 💻 Computers store numbers in binary, not decimal. Just like 1/3 becomes 0.3333… forever, numbers like 0.1 have repeating binary representations. IEEE 754 floating-point numbers have limited precision, so the computer stores the closest representable value instead. That’s why in languages like Python and JavaScript: 0.1 + 0.2 !== 0.3 😳 Usually harmless. But tiny errors can become dangerous when they accumulate over time. 🚨 In 1991, a Patriot missile system in Saudi Arabia suffered a timing error after running for around 100 hours. The accumulated drift contributed to its failure to track an incoming Scud missile. The missile struck a barracks, killing 28 soldiers. 🔥 How developers avoid these problems: ✅ Use integers for money, such as cents. ✅ Use exact decimal types when appropriate, like Java’s BigDecimal or Python’s Decimal. ✅ Compare floating-point numbers using a tolerance instead of exact equality. One tiny rounding error can teach a massive lesson about software engineering. 💬 Want to learn how banks handle precision in financial systems? author: invokedynamics
text: Vibecoder vs Real Coder #larp #vibecoder #code #coder A vibe coder is someone who builds software, apps, or websites by using natural language prompts to direct artificial intelligence rather than writing code manually. How Vibe Coding Works • Intent-Driven Development: Instead of typing syntax line-by-line, the creator tells an AI what they want in plain English (e.g., "Build a budgeting app with a login system"). • The AI Loop: The AI generates the code, structure, and database, and the user tests the output, spots errors, and feeds the feedback back into the model until the app works. • "Forgetting the Code": Coined by AI researcher Andrej Karpathy in early 2025, the term describes a style where the builder completely detaches from the underlying source code, focusing only on the "vibe" and final user experience.

author: rick.theengineer
text: Every time you hit send on WhatsApp, your message goes on a journey most people never see. 👀 Here's the whole backend roadmap in under 3 minutes, built from scratch, one stop at a time: 01 → Server: your app has to run somewhere (Java, Go, Python, JavaScript…) 02 → API: the contract your phone uses to talk to the server (POST /messages) 03 → Database: where your messages actually live (PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB) 04 → Cache: Redis keeps hot data in memory so millions of users don't melt your database 05 → WebSockets: one open connection, so messages arrive in real time 06 → Message Queue: the sender doesn't wait while a background worker sends the push notification 07 → Load Balancer: one server isn't enough, so traffic gets spread across many 08 → Containers: Docker packages your app, Kubernetes runs it across machines 09 → Architecture: monolith vs microservices (spoiler: microservices aren't automatically better) 10 → Observability: metrics, logs and traces show what's really happening inside The big lesson: backend engineering isn't just writing endpoints. It's designing systems that stay secure, reliable and fast when millions of people use them. Watch it twice. The second time, follow the green message the whole way through. 💬 Which stop are you at on your roadmap right now? Drop the number below 👇 Save this for your next system design interview, and send it to someone learning to code. #backendengineering #systemdesign #softwareengineering #webdevelopment #learntocode

author: legitalgorithmswithpeter
text: 💀 One wrong command deleted 300GB of production data. And EVERY backup had failed. This actually happened to GitLab in 2017. 🤯 An engineer was trying to fix a broken database replica. After hours of troubleshooting, he ran a command to wipe the data directory. But he was on the WRONG server. The live production database was gone. And then things got even worse. 🚨 💾 Cloud backups? Broken because of incompatible PostgreSQL tools. 📧 Warning emails? Never delivered. 🖥️ Disk snapshots? Not enabled for the database servers. 🔄 Database replica? Already wiped. GitLab had multiple backup strategies, but none could reliably save them. Then, pure luck saved the day. An engineer had copied a recent database snapshot to a staging server just hours earlier. GitLab recovered, but around six hours of database activity was permanently lost. 🔥 The biggest lesson? A backup you have never tested restoring isn’t a backup. It’s just hope. 💬 When was the last time you tested your backups? #GitLab #Database #DevOps #SystemDesign #SoftwareEngineering

author: legitalgorithmswithpeter
text: Vibe Coding vs Real Software Engineering 🤖💻 The debate isn’t “AI writes bad code.” It’s that AI can write code that looks correct while violating the actual intent. LLMs predict plausible tokens — they don’t verify business logic, security, concurrency, or correctness. That creates risks like: 📦 Package hallucination → AI recommends packages that don’t exist. ☠️ Slopsquatting → Attackers register those names and publish malicious packages. And the senior vs junior gap matters. A senior engineer can spot a broken authorization check or race condition because they’ve seen similar failures before. A junior may not have that mental library yet — making AI confidence look like correctness. The same problem appears during debugging: if you didn’t design the code, you first have to reconstruct why it exists before figuring out why it broke. Vibe coding makes sense for prototypes and low-stakes tools. But production systems still need architecture, review, testing, and verification. And teams are increasingly using property-based testing and fuzzing to test generated code across huge input spaces. The real question: If AI writes the code juniors used to learn from, where does the next generation of senior engineers come from? 👀 #VibeCoding #AIProgramming #SoftwareEngineering #AIEngineering #DeveloperSkills

text: ⚔️ React vs Next.js — Is Next.js actually a replacement for React? 🤯 No! Next.js is built ON TOP of React. Every Next.js app uses React. Think of React as a car engine. Next.js is the complete car, with everything else you need to drive. 🚗💨 🔥 Here’s what makes them different: ⚛️ React: A JavaScript library for building user interfaces. You choose additional tools for routing, rendering, and other features. 🚀 Next.js: A full React framework with routing, server rendering, static generation, and built-in optimizations. 🌐 SEO & Performance: Next.js supports multiple rendering strategies to help deliver content faster and improve search visibility. 🗂️ Routing: React typically needs a separate routing library. Next.js uses file-based routing. 🖥️ Backend: Next.js supports server-side logic and API endpoints, while React alone focuses on the UI. 🎯 Which should you choose? Use React for interactive dashboards and internal tools. Choose Next.js for blogs, e-commerce stores, and public websites that benefit from SEO and server rendering. 💡 The bottom line: Learn React first. Next.js adds the framework and tools to build complete web applications. 💬 Are you Team React or Team Next.js? #React #NextJS #JavaScript #WebDevelopment #Programming

author: machinelearningtogo
text: ➡️ Part 1 of Machine Learning & AI simply explained Concepts, no code: what AI is, what machine learning adds, and how the two fit together. Two questions guide the video: what even is AI, and what makes machine learning different? Step 1, AI. Short for artificial intelligence, AI is a big goal: computers that do things we would call smart, like playing chess, understanding speech or driving a car. Step 2, rules by hand. For decades, people built AI by writing every rule themselves. If this happens, then do that. That works for a game like chess. It falls apart for spotting a cat in a photo, because no list of rules covers a cat hiding behind a sofa. Step 3, machine learning. Machine learning builds AI from examples. You show the computer thousands of pictures, each labeled cat or not cat, and it works out the rules by itself. Step 4, how they fit together. AI is the goal, and machine learning is one way to reach it, the way that learns from data. Inside machine learning sits deep learning, which uses neural networks with many layers. Inside deep learning sit chatbots like ChatGPT, large language models trained on huge amounts of text. Step 5, why they get mixed up. Almost every AI in the news today uses machine learning, so people treat the two words like one. A chess program built only from hand-written rules is still AI, with no learning inside at all. The short answers. What is AI? The big goal of machines doing smart things. What is machine learning? The part of AI that finds its own rules in examples. Every machine learning system is AI. Some AI never learns anything. #machinelearning #ai #neuralnetworks #chatgpt #computerscience

author: rick.theengineer
text: Why didn't we just invent ONE programming language and use it for everything? 🤔 Everything in this video is real output. I ran it all on an actual computer 👇 💾 1950s: the quadratic formula as machine code is 49 numbers. Then FORTRAN let scientists write it in ONE line, the way they'd write it on paper. 🏦 1959: COBOL was built for business records: banks, payroll, accounting. Already two languages, two completely different problems. ⚙️ 1972: C gave programmers raw control over memory… and the power to crash. Overflow an 8-byte buffer and the program jumps to address 0x4141414141414141. That's the letter "A", typed by the user. That's how programs get hacked. ☕ Java promised "write once, run anywhere" and cleaned up memory automatically. 🐍 Python bet on simplicity: 8 lines of Java become 1 line of Python… but on the same loop, Python took 3.886 s while C took 0.032 s. That's 121× slower. 🦀 Rust refuses to compile memory bugs at all. The program never even runs, yet it's almost as fast as C. So why not combine everything into one perfect language? Because every design choice is a trade-off: control vs safety, simplicity vs power, automatic memory vs maximum speed. You can't max both ends of the same slider. Languages didn't multiply because engineers couldn't agree on syntax. They multiplied because computing kept creating new problems 🔁 Which language did you learn first, and which one do you actually use today? Tell me below 👇 Save this for the next time someone asks "which language should I learn?" 📌 #programming #coding #computerscience #softwareengineering #techhistory

So verbrennst du jede Woche Stunden mit Suchen und Planen, die Claude längst für dich erledigen könnte. Deshalb der bessere Weg mit 4 Claude-Systemen: Erstens ein Lebenspanel, das Kalender, Mails und Aufgaben auf eine Seite zieht und dir jeden Morgen eine Zusammenfassung schickt. Zweitens ein Finanzberater, der dir sagt, wo du dein Budget überziehst, wie viel bis zum Sparziel fehlt, und dich vor wichtigen Zahlungen warnt. Drittens ein Gym- und Ernährungscoach, bei dem Claude Routine und Menüs an deinen Fortschritt anpasst. Viertens ein zweites Gehirn: Verträge, Versicherungen, PDFs und Notizen rein, und Claude sagt dir sofort, wann deine Versicherung abläuft. Den Teil hat gerade noch fast niemand auf dem Schirm. Weil jedes System ein paar Einstellungen in Claude braucht, die man leicht übersieht, hab ich dir einen kompletten Guide gemacht: Schritt für Schritt, mit allen 4 Systemen, den exakten Prompts für jedes Projekt und dem Setup für Kalender und Mails. Wenn du ihn willst: kommentiere „Leben", folge, und ich schick's dir garantiert zu.

author: meycuanc
text: Parte 2: cómo crear tu Design System en Claude 💻 Si ya hiciste tu branding en ChatGPT, ahora toca convertirlo en reglas para que tus carruseles, presentaciones y diseños no parezcan de marcas diferentes cada vez 😭 Paso 1. Pídele a ChatGPT un resumen de tu marca: “Hazme un resumen de mi marca con qué hace, para quién es, personalidad, tono, colores, tipografías, estilo visual y qué cosas debe evitar. No inventes nada nuevo; usa únicamente lo que ya construimos.” Paso 2. Descarga tu moodboard. Paso 3. Guarda 3–5 referencias de carruseles o diseños que representen el estilo que quieres conseguir. No es para copiarlos. Son para que Claude entienda cosas como composición, jerarquías, tamaño de títulos, uso de fotos, cantidad de texto, etc. Paso 4. Sube a Claude: • resumen de marca • moodboard • referencias de diseño Y usa este prompt: “Voy a darte tres cosas: un resumen escrito de mi marca, un moodboard visual y varios ejemplos de carruseles y diseños cuyo estilo me gusta. Quiero que uses el resumen para entender la personalidad, público, propósito, tono y valores de la marca. Usa el moodboard para entender la identidad visual ya definida: colores, tipografías, logo, estilo, dirección visual y sensación general. Y usa los ejemplos de carruseles y diseños para entender cómo quiero que esa identidad se vea aplicada en piezas reales: composición, jerarquía, distribución, ritmo, uso de imágenes, cantidad de texto y estilo de cada slide. No copies literalmente los diseños de referencia y no inventes una nueva identidad. A partir de todo esto, crea un Design System completo para mi marca. Define de forma clara: * paleta de color y cómo usarla * tipografías y jerarquías * tamaños y proporciones de títulos, subtítulos y texto * espaciado, márgenes y distribución * estilo fotográfico * composición de carruseles y portadas * uso de iconos, formas y elementos gráficos * cantidad recomendada de texto por slide * tipos de layouts que se pueden repetir * reglas para mantener coherencia entre diferentes piezas * cosas que nunca deben aparecer en los diseños Quiero que el sistema sea práctico y pensado para crear carruseles, presentaciones, portadas y contenido para redes sociales. Al final, incluye ejemplos de cómo aplicar el sistema en: 1. una portada 2. un slide con mucho texto 3. un slide con fotografía 4. un slide con datos o cifras. Todo debe sentirse como la misma marca.” Paso 5. Pruébalo. Pídele a Claude que cree un carrusel usando únicamente ese Design System y empieza a corregir: “Quiero títulos más grandes.” “Esto se siente muy corporativo.” “Usa menos elementos.” “Deja más espacio.” “Este tipo de fotografía sí, este no.” Y cuando algo te guste: “Agrega esto como una regla permanente de mi Design System.” Ahí es donde realmente se pone bueno, porque ya no tienes que volver a explicar cómo quieres que se vea tu marca cada vez que creas algo. Guárdalo porque este es de esos procesos que haces una vez y después te ahorra muchísimo tiempo. 👩‍💻✨ #claude #claudeai #inteligenciaartificial #aprendizajecontinuo #mujereslatinas

text: AI pracovala sedem dní sama. Nikto jej medzitým nehovoril, čo má robiť ďalej. Firma Cursor, ktorá robí nástroj na programovanie s umelou inteligenciou, dala svojim AI agentom jednu veľkú úlohu. Napísať internetový prehliadač, teda program, cez ktorý chodíš na internet. A potom ich nechala bežať takmer celý týždeň. Zaujímavé na tom nie je ani tak to, čo z toho vzniklo, ale ako to vznikalo. Agenti si sami rozplánovali prácu, písali kód, spúšťali testy, našli chyby a opravovali ich. Človek nezasahoval takmer vôbec. Za ten čas napísali vyše milióna riadkov kódu v tisícke súborov. To video hore je záznam tej práce. Každý bod je jeden súbor a vidíš, ako projekt rastie hodinu po hodine. Doteraz AI dobre zvládala krátke úlohy. Napíš mi text, oprav mi túto funkciu, zhrň mi tento dokument. Toto je iná liga. Týždeň znamená, že si systém musí pamätať, čo robil v pondelok, keď je piatok, a nestratiť pritom smer. Férovo treba dodať aj druhú stranu. Prehliadač zatiaľ nefunguje tak, ako má, a vývojári, ktorí si ho stiahli, hlásia chyby pri spúšťaní. Šéf firmy sám povedal, že to “akosi” funguje a že k použiteľnému prehliadaču má ďaleko. A nebol to jeden agent, ako sa píše na sieťach, ale stovky naraz. Ale otázka, ktorú ten experiment otvára, nie je o prehliadači. Je o tom, či sa práca časom nezmení tak, že človek bude určovať smer a vykonávať to budú agenti. Čo myslíš, koľko to potrvá? Napíš do komentárov. Zdroje: Cursor, GIGAZINE, 36Kr #ai #umelainteligencia #cursor #aiagent

text: Software engineering isn’t just “writing code” 👀 It’s the process of designing, building, testing, and maintaining software that actually solves real problems. When you open an app, book a flight, send a payment, or scroll a website… that’s software engineering in action. So where does web development fit in? Web development is a branch of software engineering focused on building applications that run in the browser (and on servers behind them). Frontend engineers handle what users see and interact with. Backend engineers handle logic, databases, authentication, APIs. Together, they apply the same engineering principles: clean architecture, version control, testing, scalability, security. That’s why web development isn’t “just websites.” It’s building full software systems… delivered through the web. If you’re learning HTML, CSS, JavaScript… you’re already stepping into software engineering. #softwareengineering #webdevelopment #programming #coding #developerlife

author: kodekloud
text: Interview: How Browser Cookies Actually Work When you sign into a website like Apple and close your browser, you stay logged in because of browser cookies. During login, the server generates a unique session ID in its database and delivers it to your browser inside an HTTP Set-Cookie response header. A cookie is simply a small piece of text containing a key and value, guarded by strict browser directives like Secure to enforce encrypted HTTPS transmission and HttpOnly to stop malicious scripts from stealing your session token. On your next visit, your browser automatically attaches this saved cookie to your request, allowing the server to recognize your account and shopping cart instantly without asking for your password again. Cookies become controversial when third-party advertising networks use them to follow you across the internet. When an external ad provider loads banners across thousands of unrelated websites, it reads the same third-party tracking cookie to assemble a detailed profile of your browsing habits. This widespread tracking is why privacy regulations like GDPR force websites to show consent banners for marketing trackers, even while essential login cookies quietly do their job in the background. While attackers can impersonate you if they steal an active session cookie, these tiny text files remain the indispensable glue that keeps your daily digital life connected. #WebDevelopment #CyberSecurity #SoftwareEngineering #TechExplained #SystemDesign #CodingForBeginners

author: pro.glitch
text: Build a second brain with Claude You save the article. You write the meeting notes. You keep the customer email. Three weeks later you can't find any of it. Here's the second brain I'd build instead. Three pieces: A folder of plain text files on your computer. You own it. Obsidian opens the folder and shows the files and the links between them as a map. That's where you read. Claude Code opens the same folder and does all the writing. Inside the folder: raw (everything you drop in, never edited), wiki (pages Claude writes and keeps current, each linking back to its sources) and CLAUDE.md (the rulebook). Three jobs. Ingest: drop in Monday's call notes and one call updates five pages. Ask: every answer points to the raw note it came from. Lint: once a week the brain checks itself for pages that disagree, orphan pages and numbers with no source. The rules that stop the confident nonsense: no source, no number. Every claim tagged as extracted or inferred. Little data means "early signal", not fact. Old claims get marked outdated, never deleted. Start with one client, one project, or your own business. #claudecode #aiautomation #aiagents #aiemployee

text: Most software engineers know that the first example has a linear O(n) space complexity due to the space consumed on the call stack, but far less know the space complexity of the second example. 🧠 ANSWER: O(n) That's right. The second example ALSO has an O(n) space complexity. Although the second example has two recursive calls in it, the space consumed on the call stack remains the same.  How could this be? Since the second example makes more recursive calls, shouldn't it consume more stack space? Nope.  The key is that the maximum stack depth is the same for both. The first example forms a recursive chain like: 2 | 1 | 0 The second example forms a recursive tree like: ⠀⠀⠀2 ⠀⠀/⠀⠀\ ⠀1⠀⠀⠀1 ⠀/ \⠀⠀ / \ 0⠀0⠀ 0⠀0 The depth of both of these structures is identical. 🚨👀 For a fully animated explanation of how the call stack works go to my page and watch reel titled "EP 6 Call Stack & Space Complexity DSA Explained"  #coding #leetcode #softwareengineer #computerscience #softwareengineering [software engineer, leetcode, coding, computer science, software engineering, cs major, data structures and algorithms]

text: Business owner, if you think vibe coding means you can build your own software and cancel the tools you pay for, the front end is the easy part. Everyone says SaaS is going to be dead. Vibe coding is going to take over everything. I don't think so. So will vibe coding kill SaaS in 2026? My view: no. Because there's so much that goes into real software. Here's where vibe coding works: - Building a prototype - Building something for yourself - Building something for internal purposes That's great. But even for that, you still need skills. It's not like anybody can just open Claude Code and start building something that holds up. Here's what vibe coding doesn't solve for you: 1. The back end. You'll be able to build the front end. The back end is going to be a problem. 2. Maintenance. That's going to be a problem too. 3. Connection to other tools. Your software has to work with the rest of your business. 4. Security. In my view, this is the most important one. Security is becoming a big issue now. Thinking about building your own app with AI? Ask yourself four questions first. Step 1: Can I build the back end, not just the front end? Step 2: Who is going to maintain it? Step 3: How will it connect to my other tools? Step 4: How will I keep it secure? Vibe coding is a great start. It just isn't the whole job. Learn to build with AI properly, with the skills that go past the prototype. Join me at aileadbuilder.com #vibecoding #aicoding #saas #claudecode #aiforbusiness

author: alanonai
text: People ask me all the time how I code with AI. Here's the short answer. I use Claude Code. But the code is the AI's job. My job is the decisions. And I keep three habits on every app I build, even the little ones I make for myself on a Saturday. One. Know which decisions are yours. Before it builds anything, ask the AI what has to be decided first. Read the list. Answer the ones that matter to you. Two. Read what you build on. Whatever it hands you before it starts building, read it. Actually read it. A wrong sentence is one sentence to fix before it's built, and a lot more after. Three. Verify, don't ask. If your app has logins, or anyone's information but your own, check it yourself. Log in as the wrong person and try. A confident yes from the AI that built it proves nothing. That's the floor. Everything else depends on one question. What happens if it's wrong? If it's just for you, those three habits are plenty. If clients are logging in with private files, you want a lot more. That's the short version. The long version is a sixteen-part series, and this is the last one. Series is called Build with AI. This article is "How Much of This Do You Actually Need?" Link's in comments. #ai #vibecoding #programming #coding

author: dopaminedevs
text: The expensive part of AI code was never writing it. It's reading it, reviewing it and owning it for years. Ponytail (a Claude Code plugin by DietrichGebert) is built on that idea: every line an agent adds is a line you now maintain, so the best diff is often the smallest one. Ask for a date picker and a default agent writes 335 lines. Ponytail writes 10. Version 5 pushes it further. A review command that finds what the diff hides, an audit that ranks the whole repo by what to fix first, and a live band for cost, tokens and tests (Claude Code only). The headline numbers, 53% less code, 41% less time, 98% of risky logic tested, are the project's own, from 39 tasks. Not an independent benchmark. Worth testing on your own repo before you trust them. Install: /plugin marketplace add DietrichGebert/ponytail, then /plugin install ponytail@ponytail When your agent can write anything, is restraint the skill you want it to have? Repo: github.com/DietrichGebert/ponytail  #claudecode #aicoding #vibecoding #opensource #devtools

author: jbatten_builds
text: If you’re trying to get into vibecoding, please don’t let these tools trick you into thinking you don’t need a brain anymore 😂 For me, the two tools I recommend starting with are Cursor and Antigravity. 	•	Cursor is just a straight-up beast. I have not met an AI dev tool that really tops it yet. 	•	Antigravity is newer, fun, and the way it organizes files is actually clutch for new vibecoders who get overwhelmed by messy projects. But real talk: it does not matter what tool you start with if your back end is chaos. Before you get cute on the front end, you need to know: 	•	What are you using for auth? 	•	What are you using for your database? 	•	What’s your actual back-end stack? 	•	How are you going to deploy this thing? If you fuck up the back end, it truly won’t matter how pretty your UI is. As vibecoders, we already have a ton of knowledge gaps, and you cannot outsource that to AI. If every single prompt you send is full of words, tools, and dependencies you don’t understand, that’s your sign to stop prompting and go learn. The agent is not “thinking with you,” it’s just blindly implementing. You’re building a house on mud and vibes. 🧠 Slow down to speed up. Also: get your naming together. File names, function names, API names, folders — all that. If your shit is called test2-final-FINAL.js and newnewnew-api-fixed.js, you’re going to suffer later. And AI agents will too. If they can’t find the real file, they WILL make one up, and now you have duplicates, broken paths, and confusion on top of confusion. As a vibecoder, part of your “job” is: 	•	Doing cleanup days 	•	Fixing defects 	•	Organizing files 	•	Writing or updating docs Because once these agents get in your repo, they touch everything whether you meant for them to or not. This shit is powerful, but it’s not magic. You are still the engineer of record, even if the code came from an AI. 👇🏾 Are you vibecoding right now? What tools are you using—Cursor, Antigravity, Claude, Gemini, straight ChatGPT? And be honest: do you actually know what your back end is running on, or are you just hoping it doesn’t crash?  #swe #vibecoder #cursor #antigravity #opus

author: rockseerfinance
text: Anthropic could spend as much as $750 billion in the coming years to secure additional computing capacity, according to an October 20 report by The Wall Street Journal citing a draft IPO prospectus. The figure includes deals still under negotiation. It is not money already spent, nor should it be presented as a finalized investment budget. According to the report, the company behind Claude generated $16.3 billion in revenue in the first half of 2026, up from $1.1 billion a year earlier. Spending on AI infrastructure rose to nearly $9 billion during the same period. The Journal also reported a first-half net loss of $80.7 billion. Reuters, citing the Journal, said approximately $72 billion of that loss came from accounting charges tied to changes in the value of financial instruments issued to raise money—not simply cash spent operating or training AI models. The disclosures highlight the tension between fast-growing demand for AI services and the cost of securing the infrastructure needed to supply them. Anthropic did not respond to Reuters’ request for comment. Reuters said it could not immediately verify the Journal’s report. Sources: The Wall Street Journal and Reuters, October 20, 2026. #Anthropic #Claude #ArtificialIntelligence #CloudComputing #businessnews

text: Anthropic is setting aside 5% of its shares for a new public benefit fund. On CNBC Kate Rooney said that stake could be worth at least $50 billion and up to $100 billion if Anthropic debuts around $2 trillion. What Happened: Anthropic announced it Sunday and stockholders still have to approve it. The board can add 2% for every 50% rise in value above a baseline it hasn't disclosed. The fund is an Anthropic-owned LLC and its equity can't be used for lobbying or political donations. The money could go to nonprofits or to workers hurt by AI. The Reframe: It works like an executive pay package where more equity gets added as the valuation climbs. Anthropic makes that comparison itself. Every other shareholder would otherwise split the fund's stake. The Catch: Anthropic keeps control. Later in the segment Rooney noted the board decides where the money goes. Elon Musk recommended on X "giving the shares directly to the public." Rooney also said the fund could "garner some goodwill" as a reported November IPO sets up a record windfall for founders and employees. My Take: I'm counting the fund as a real cost of this IPO. That cost can grow at the board's discretion in the exact scenario you're buying for. The baseline and the fund's governance are still unpublished. I'd want both before the shares trade. text: AI assisted software development takes more than a working patch. Using AI for software architecture means keeping the whole platform in view while the implementation moves quickly. Tuesday calls this maintaining altitude. Start with the system’s purpose, governing rules, dependencies, and ownership boundaries. Then trace the problem down to the layer that should change. A local fix can look correct while leaving the same architectural failure available elsewhere. This episode explains a practical workflow for building with AI: recover the current project state, investigate before editing, revise the platform plan from evidence, and implement in manageable pieces. Then review the actual source changes, test output, and runtime behavior, not only the completion summary. Two AI models agreeing can help, but both can overlook the same dependency. Your experience matters in the questions you ask and the evidence you require. Save this for your next coding session. text: Anthropic’s Public Benefit Fund could help people—and be very good business. Convenient how that works. The company behind Claude AI plans to commit 5% of its shares to the fund, pending shareholder approval. Potential uses include nonprofit donations and support for people affected by AI-driven job disruption. The detail worth reading twice: the fund will be an LLC wholly owned by Anthropic. More governance details are still coming. A public-benefit mission doesn’t automatically give the public control. (anthropic.com) My read: ahead of Anthropic’s planned IPO, sharing the upside could help reduce resistance to the company generating it. That’s a potential business incentive, even if the giving delivers real benefits. (investing.com) A day later, Elon Musk pledged one SpaceX share for every American child in 2027. Implementation details remain unclear. (abcnews.com) Two approaches to AI wealth distribution: company-directed giving and direct ownership. Both could give beneficiaries a financial interest in the company’s success. But stock-based generosity isn’t guaranteed income. Share prices fluctuate. Rent remains annoyingly consistent. Researching AI philanthropy? Track: • Who controls distributions? • Do displaced workers actually qualify? • When does pledged equity become usable support? The useful measure is what reaches people—not how impressive the announcement sounds. #Anthropic #ArtificialIntelligence #SpaceX #FutureOfWork #AIInvesting

text: I think we’re going to see a BIG difference between people who use AI to get better at what they do and people who use it to avoid learning how to do it. And I think this applies to just about every industry, not just content creation. One of my favorite things about AI is that it gives you access to knowledge and feedback that previously might have required hiring a consultant, taking a course, or spending years figuring something out through trial and error. That’s an incredible opportunity if you’re willing to actually learn from it. But I do worry that we’re going to get so accustomed to outsourcing every little task that we stop developing some of those skills ourselves. I’m a huge advocate for using AI as much as possible. And we SHOULD know how to use the tool to make our daily tasks better. I just think we should be intentional about how we’re using it. I’m curious where everyone lands on this, especially content creators. author: techsensedev
text: The tests pass. The demo works. Then someone asks you to walk through the code, and you realize you can't. A Hacker News thread asking how to deal with shipping AI-written code you don't understand drew 698 comments. One commenter's fix: you design the abstractions and how the pieces talk to each other, and the AI only fills in the units. You might not know every line, but you know what every piece is for. Another commenter shared a friend's phrase for code that is wrong at every level: "fractally busted". Our take at Techsense Developers: if nobody on the team can explain it, it isn't ready for production, no matter who or what wrote it. #softwareengineering #codereview #devlife

author: presailapp
text: Presailapp.com #creatorsearchinsights #smallcontentcreators #vibecoding #app #newaccountontiktok  Presail AI is a security platform designed to help developers, founders, and entrepreneurs identify potential vulnerabilities in their applications before those weaknesses become serious problems. As AI-powered coding platforms such as Base44, Lovable, Bolt, and other vibe-coding tools make it easier than ever to build and launch software without extensive programming experience, more people are publishing applications without necessarily understanding the security risks behind them. Presail aims to address this problem by making application security more accessible, understandable, and actionable, especially for indie hackers, SaaS founders, startups, and nontechnical builders who want to launch confidently without needing to become cybersecurity experts. Instead of expecting users to manually inspect code, understand complicated security terminology, or hire expensive security professionals for every early-stage project, Presail provides a streamlined experience in which users can submit or scan their applications, receive an analysis of potential security issues, and understand what those findings could mean for their product and its users. The platform’s goal is not simply to display a list of technical warnings, but to help developers understand which issues deserve attention, why they matter, and what steps they can take to address them. Security problems can include improperly exposed secrets, insecure access controls, weaknesses in authentication, potentially vulnerable application logic, misconfigured permissions, and other issues that could put sensitive information or application functionality at risk, depending on what the platform’s scanning capabilities support. Presail is being developed around the idea that security should be considered before an application gains users, collects sensitive information, or becomes a real business, rather than treated as an afterthought once something goes wrong. Its intended value is especially relevant to people who move quickly from idea to prototype to launch and may not have a dedicated security team to review their work. By combining a straightforward interface, an approachable scanning experience, and useful explanations of findings, Presail aims to make security testing feel less intimidating and more practical for everyday builders. The broader vision is to become a trusted security companion for the growing ecosystem of AI-assisted software development, helping independent creators and growing companies make more informed decisions about the applications they build and publish. Presail is not intended to replace a comprehensive professional penetration test, a qualified security engineer, or every other layer of a mature security program; rather, its purpose is to make identifying and understanding potential security weaknesses more accessible during development and before launch. Ultimately, Presail AI is built around one core belief: building software has become dramatically easier, but making sure that software is secure still matters just as much. By helping close the gap between rapid application development and security awareness, Presail aims to give developers a clearer path toward building, improving, and launching software with greater confidence.
